23.headline: W23 demand $70.0K, +14.4% YoY. Three retention warnings open the period.
23.summary: Three retention warnings open the period. Returning customers were flat at 159 vs 159, returning Gen Z fell to 17 from 26 (-34.6%), and only 4.5% of new Gen Z joined Insider. W23 is the first week in the extract, so L4W and period-to-date equal this one week and the inventory rules stay off until the four-week window fills. Demand grew +14.4% YoY to $70.0K (LY $61.2K), with transactions +6.6% and AOV +7.3% at $311.32. Gen Z new customers were 22 vs 15 (+46.7%), 33.3% of all new customers vs 28.8% last year. Tabby led growth with +10.5 pts of contribution (+70.8% YoY), while Trench was the largest drag at -3.0 pts (-67.9%). Trench also shows 32.5 weeks of supply on a one-week sales window, a watch item rather than an alert.

24.headline: W24 demand $75.2K, +9.1% YoY on bigger baskets, while transactions fell 2.9%.
24.summary: Transactions fell -2.9% YoY in W24, but demand still grew +9.1% to $75.2K because AOV rose +12.4% to $321.57, so this was a basket week, not a traffic week. The retention proxies stayed weak over W23–W24: returning customers -2.7%, returning Gen Z 36 vs 51 (-29.4%), and only 16.3% of new Gen Z joined Insider. Gen Z new customers were 21 vs 16 (+31.3%), 32.8% of new customers vs 25.8% last year. Demand is +7.4% WoW and +11.6% period-to-date. Tabby added +14.1 pts of growth (+109%), while Tailored Jacket was the biggest drag (-3.0 pts, -63.3%) and holds 22.4 weeks of supply. Tabby cover is down to 5.1 weeks vs 11.4 LY on a sales window that is still truncated, so no stock rule fires yet.

25.headline: W25 demand $62.9K, +8.3% YoY, but down 16.4% on the week as traffic dipped.
25.summary: Demand fell -16.4% WoW in W25, and this time it is traffic: transactions -12.8% WoW while AOV slipped only -4.1%. Against last year the week still grew +8.3% ($62.9K vs $58.1K), and period-to-date demand is +10.6%. Retention proxies remain the weak spot over W23–W25: returning customers -5.1% (463 vs 488), returning Gen Z 49 vs 67 (-26.9%), and new Gen Z Insider attach 19.4%. Acquisition is the bright spot: 29 Gen Z new customers vs 12 (+142%), 41.4% of all new vs 24.0% LY. Tabby (+11.9 pts, +75.2%) and Pillow Tabby (+4.1 pts, +172%) carry the growth, while Tailored Jacket is -59.5%. Tabby cover is already 4.5 weeks vs 9.6 LY, though the window is still truncated, so there is no stock alert yet.

29.headline: W29 demand $71.3K, +12.7% YoY. Two critical stock alerts on the Tabby franchise.
29.summary: Pillow Tabby is down to 1.8 weeks of supply and Tabby to 2.1, against 5.1 and 7.0 last year, with only 27 and 92 units left. These are the period's growth leaders, so stock is the decision this week. Demand was +12.7% YoY ($71.3K vs $63.3K) on transactions +14.7%. The -18.8% WoW drop is basket, not traffic: transactions -2.3% WoW and AOV -16.9% after the W28 spike. L4W demand is +13.2% and period-to-date +12.1%. Gen Z new customers were 41 vs 16 (+156%), 47.1% of new vs 27.6% LY, and 140 vs 60 over L4W (+133%). But only 16.4% of new Gen Z joined Insider over L4W. Halo apparel is the drag: Knit Dress -62.7% and Rogue -35.9% over L4W, with Knit Dress holding 20.7 weeks of supply.

system_prompts.summary: You write a weekly retail performance summary for a merchandising leadership team. Use ONLY numbers that appear in the JSON facts. Do not compute, round differently, or infer new numbers (no differences, ratios, sums or 'x times'). Percent fields are fractions; render 0.1265 as 12.7% (YoY above 100% as a whole percent, e.g. 1.5625 → +156%). Money as $71.3K. Weeks of supply to 1 decimal. Lead with the most severe anomaly (critical > warning > info). Say 'L4W' and 'period-to-date' for windows. Plain prose, one paragraph, no headings or bullets. Max 180 words.
system_prompts.headline: You write the masthead headline of a weekly retail dashboard: at most two short sentences, about 15 words. First the week's result (demand and its YoY), then the single most severe alert. State results; never address the reader. Use ONLY numbers that appear in the JSON facts, formatted as in the summary rules ($71.3K, +12.7%).
system_prompts.card: You write one briefing card for a retail analytics agent, in its voice: first person, calm, specific. Return JSON {"headline": str, "body": str}. Headline: ONE sentence that states what happened with the key numbers in it (max 22 words). Body: 2-3 short sentences: why it matters, the evidence, what to do. Use ONLY numbers that appear in the card's `values`. Do not compute, round differently, or infer new numbers. Percent fields are fractions (0.2826 → 28%, or 28.3%). *_pts fields are percentage points (+5.0 pts). Weeks of supply to 1 decimal. Money as $23.1K. You may cite finding IDs (F11) and recommendation IDs (R1).
